The periodic background refreshing lives in the CLI scheduler package. Here's the full chain:

## The periodic loop

`feedScheduler` — `internal/cli/scheduler.go:33-51` is the actual background loop:

```go
for range time.Tick(frequency) {
    jobs, err := store.NewBatchBuilder().
        WithBatchSize(batchSize).
        WithErrorLimit(errorLimit).
        WithoutDisabledFeeds().
        WithNextCheckExpired().
        WithLimitPerHost(limitPerHost).
        FetchJobs()
    ...
    pool.Push(jobs)
}
```

It ticks every `PollingFrequency` and selects only feeds whose `next_check` has expired (`WithNextCheckExpired`), skipping disabled feeds and respecting per-host limits, then hands the batch to the worker pool.

## How it gets started

`startDaemon` — `internal/cli/daemon.go:23-37` creates the pool and starts the scheduler:

```go
pool := worker.NewPool(store, config.Opts.WorkerPoolSize())

if config.Opts.HasSchedulerService() && !config.Opts.HasMaintenanceMode() {
    runScheduler(store, pool)
}
```

`runScheduler` — `internal/cli/scheduler.go:15-31` launches `feedScheduler` as a goroutine (alongside `cleanupScheduler`).

## Execution of each job

- `Pool.Push` — `internal/worker/pool.go:23-31` feeds an unbuffered channel.
- `worker.Run` — `internal/worker/worker.go:24-57` loops on that channel and calls `feedHandler.RefreshFeed(w.store, job.UserID, job.FeedID, false)` per job (line 47), recording `metric.BackgroundFeedRefreshDuration` when metrics are enabled.
- `NewPool` — `internal/worker/pool.go:42-55` spins up `WorkerPoolSize()` of those workers.

## What decides *when* a given feed is due

`Feed.ScheduleNextCheck` — `internal/model/feed.go:123-150` computes the next interval: either the round-robin `SchedulerRoundRobinMinInterval` or, in entry-frequency mode, `(7*24h) / (weeklyCount * factor)` capped at `SchedulerEntryFrequencyMaxInterval`. So the tick frequency is uniform, but each feed's `next_check` makes the effective refresh rate per-feed.

## Two similar-but-different code paths (easy to confuse)

- `refreshFeeds` — `internal/cli/refresh_feeds.go:17-77` is the *one-shot* CLI command (`miniflux -refresh-feeds`): same batch builder, but it spawns its own temporary worker goroutines over a local `jobQueue` and exits — no ticker.
